subject.title: refactor(channels): move inbound turn execution into core

question: Should the Plugin SDK expose `configOverride` as a supported resolver-only dispatch contract for channel adapters, or should Microsoft Teams keep this override behind a narrower owner-specific seam?
rationale: This is an additive external Plugin SDK surface in a compatibility-sensitive multi-channel refactor; the code is plausible, but the permanent public contract and ownership boundary require maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a narrow SDK contract
options.body: Accept `configOverride` only as a documented resolver-only merged override, with focused compatibility coverage for callers that omit it.

options.title: Keep the override owner-specific
options.body: Refactor the Teams sender-timezone adaptation behind an existing or new narrow Teams/core seam instead of exposing a general Plugin SDK field.

options.title: Pause the API addition
options.body: Land no new SDK contract until the intended external-plugin use case and deprecation/ownership plan are agreed.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow SDK contract
recommendation.body: Accept `configOverride` only as a documented resolver-only merged override, with focused compatibility coverage for callers that omit it.

likelyOwner.reason: The preceding merged lifecycle refactor and this follow-up place this contributor closest to the intended ownership boundary.
